title: What version control is and why it exists

videos.script: Look at this folder. {{folder}} Five copies of one report. Report, report v2, v2 final, v2 final Bruno, and FINAL in capitals. Nobody planned it. Each copy was a sensible thing to do on the day it was made. {{sensible}} Now answer three questions from it. Which one is current? What changed between these two? And why? {{questions}} The folder cannot tell you. It kept the old versions and lost everything about them: who changed what, when, and for what reason. {{lost}} And here is the one that does real damage. {{diverged}} Bruno fixed a figure in his copy. Somebody else fixed a different line in FINAL. Neither copy has both. Whoever sends FINAL sends it without Bruno's fix, and nothing warns them. Version control is the answer to that folder. Not better names for the copies. A history. {{history}} Every saved state of the whole project, with a name, a date and a sentence saying why, each one pointing at the one before. Git keeps that history, and it keeps all of it on your machine. {{local}} This lesson is what a history is and where it lives. By the end of it, your machine will be ready for the first commit. {{title}}
